title: Lifetime Spend Per Customer
description:
Report every customer's name and their total spend across **completed** orders only, rounded to 2 decimals. Customers with no completed orders report `0`.

Name the columns `customer` and `revenue`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price END), 0), 2) AS revenue
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
hint: Chain two LEFT JOINs so customers survive, and filter the status inside the SUM rather than in WHERE.
outputExplanation: Ada has spent $625, Cy has spent $75, and Bo and Di have spent nothing on completed orders.

title: Repeat Customers
description:
Report the name of every customer who has placed **two or more** orders, along with their order count.

Name the columns `customer` and `orders`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer, COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2;
hint: An inner join is fine here — a customer with fewer than two orders can never qualify.
outputExplanation: Ada has placed 3 orders and Cy has placed 2 — both are repeat customers. Bo has only 1 order and Di has none.

title: Revenue By Month
description:
Report total revenue for each calendar month across completed orders, rounded to 2 decimals. Format the month as `YYYY-MM`.

Name the columns `month` and `revenue`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month,
       ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
WHERE o.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY month;
hint: strftime('%Y-%m', ...) truncates a date to its month and groups neatly.
outputExplanation: Revenue from completed orders was $185 in January 2022, $300 in February 2022, $75 in March 2022, and $140 in January 2023.

title: Best Selling Product By Revenue
description:
Report the product (or products, if tied) with the highest total revenue across all order items.

Name the columns `product` and `revenue`, with revenue rounded to 2 decimals. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH totals AS (
  SELECT p.name AS product, ROUND(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 2) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  GROUP BY p.id, p.name
)
SELECT product, revenue
FROM totals
WHERE revenue = (SELECT MAX(revenue) FROM totals);
hint: Aggregate first, then compare against the maximum of that aggregate — ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 would silently drop ties.
outputExplanation: Desk generated the most revenue at $300 across all order items.

title: Each Customer's First Order
description:
For every customer who has ordered, report the date of their earliest order. If two orders share that earliest date, report the row with the smaller order id.

Name the columns `customer` and `first_order`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer, o.order_date AS first_order
FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS rn
  FROM orders
) o
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.rn = 1;
hint: ROW_NUMBER with a tie-breaker in the ORDER BY guarantees exactly one row per customer.
outputExplanation: Ada's first order was on 2022-01-10, Bo's on 2022-02-20, and Cy's on 2022-03-05. Di has never ordered.

title: Each Category's Share Of Revenue
description:
Report each product category's total revenue and its percentage of overall revenue, both rounded to 2 decimals. Ignore items whose product has no category.

Name the columns `category`, `revenue` and `pct`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT category,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * revenue / SUM(revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct
FROM (
  SELECT p.category AS category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  WHERE p.category IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.category
);
hint: Aggregate to one row per category, then use SUM(...) OVER () to reach the grand total without a second scan.
outputExplanation: Furniture accounts for 59.38% of total revenue ($570) and Tech accounts for 40.63% ($390).

title: Distinct Products Per Order
description:
Report every order that contains **two or more distinct products**, along with how many distinct products it contains.

Name the columns `order_id` and `products`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT order_id, COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS products
FROM order_items
GROUP BY order_id
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) >= 2;
hint: COUNT(DISTINCT col) inside both the SELECT and the HAVING.
outputExplanation: Orders 1 and 6 each contain two distinct products. All other orders contain only one product each.

title: Spending More Than Your Country's Average
description:
For each customer compute their total spend over all order items. Report those who spend strictly more than the average spend of customers in the same country. Customers who never ordered count as spending 0.

Name the columns `customer`, `country` and `spend`, with spend rounded to 2 decimals. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH spend AS (
  SELECT c.id, c.name, c.country,
         COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) AS total
  FROM customers c
  LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
  LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.country
)
SELECT name AS customer, country, ROUND(total, 2) AS spend
FROM (SELECT *, AVG(total) OVER (PARTITION BY country) AS country_avg FROM spend)
WHERE total > country_avg;
hint: Compute the per-customer totals first, then apply a window average over country to that derived table.
outputExplanation: Ada spends $625, well above the US average of $350. Cy ($75), Bo ($0) and Di ($0) all spend at or below their country's average.

title: Month Over Month Revenue Change
description:
For each month that has revenue, report its revenue and the change against the previous month **present in the data**. The earliest month reports NULL.

Name the columns `month`, `revenue` and `change`, with both amounts rounded to 2 decimals. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.order_date) AS month,
         SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month), 2) AS change
FROM monthly;
hint: Aggregate by month first; LAG over the aggregated rows compares each month to the previous one.
outputExplanation: Revenue rose from $185 in January 2022 to $480 in February, then fell to $155 in March, and was $140 in January 2023.

title: Priced Above Your Category
description:
Report every product priced strictly above the average price of its own category.

Name the columns `name`, `category` and `price`. Return the result in any order.
hint: PARTITION BY category turns the category average into just another column on each row.
outputExplanation: Keyboard ($80 at $52.50 average) and Desk ($300 at $172.50 average) are the pricier item in their respective categories.

title: Cancellation Rate Per Customer
description:
For every customer who has placed at least one order, report the percentage of their orders that were cancelled, rounded to 2 decimals.

Name the columns `customer` and `cancel_pct`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancel_pct
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
hint: SUM(CASE WHEN ... THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) counts conditionally; divide by COUNT(*) using 100.0 to force real division.
outputExplanation: Ada and Cy have no cancelled orders (0% each). Bo's only order was cancelled (100%).

title: Running Revenue By Date
description:
For each date on which revenue occurred, report that day's revenue and the cumulative revenue up to and including it, both rounded to 2 decimals.

Name the columns `order_date`, `daily` and `running`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
WITH daily AS (
  SELECT o.order_date, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS amount
  FROM orders o
  JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
  GROUP BY o.order_date
)
SELECT order_date,
       ROUND(amount, 2) AS daily,
       ROUND(SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY order_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS running
FROM daily;
hint: Collapse to one row per day first, otherwise the running total double-counts multi-item orders.
outputExplanation: Revenue accumulated from $185 on Jan 10 to $960 by Jan 2, 2023, with six dates showing activity.

title: Loyal To One Category
description:
Report every customer who has bought from exactly **one** product category (ignoring items whose product has no category), along with that category.

Name the columns `customer` and `category`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer, MIN(p.category) AS category
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE p.category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category) = 1;
hint: When a group has exactly one distinct value, MIN of that column is a safe way to report it.
outputExplanation: Bo has only bought from Furniture, and Cy only from Tech. Ada has bought from both categories and is excluded.

title: Average Order Value
description:
Report the average value of an order, counting only orders that contain at least one item, rounded to 2 decimals.

Name the column `aov`. The result is exactly one row.
hint: Average of per-order totals — not the average of individual line items, which is a different number.
outputExplanation: The average value across all 6 orders that have items is $160.

title: Empty Orders
description:
Report the id of every order that has no order items at all.

Name the column `order_id`. Return the result in any order.
hint: NOT EXISTS is the safest anti-join — unlike NOT IN, it is unaffected by NULLs in the subquery.
outputExplanation: Every order has at least one item, so no empty orders are reported. A hidden test includes an order with no items.

title: Days From Signup To First Order
description:
For every customer who has ordered, report how many days passed between their signup date and their first order date.

Name the columns `customer` and `days_to_first_order`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer,
       CAST(JULIANDAY(MIN(o.order_date)) - JULIANDAY(c.signup_date) AS INTEGER) AS days_to_first_order
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.signup_date;
hint: SQLite has no date subtraction operator — JULIANDAY() converts both dates to numbers you can subtract.
outputExplanation: Ada waited 370 days from signup to first order, Bo waited 345 days, and Cy's first order predates their signup by 117 days.
